title: multi-kms-hsm-mux-terraform-module with failover, drift detection, and secrets sync
creator: Aisha K. Munroe
description: Develop a reusable Terraform module that acts as a KMS/HSM integration layer for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must support multiple key backends (cloud KMS providers and HSM proxies), runtime selection and automatic failover, secrets synchronization with Vault and AWS Secrets Manager, drift detection probes, and upgrade-safe key rotation tooling. This ticket covers design, implementation scaffolding, CI integration, and an initial canary rollout plan for on-prem and VPC customers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module takes provider definitions for primary and secondary KMS backends and exposes a single key resource used by Redwood services
Automatic runtime failover policy configurable via inputs (priority, healthcheck timeout, cooldown) documented and covered by unit tests
Secrets sync component provides idempotent mapping between Vault paths and Secrets Manager secrets with change detection and reconcile loop
Healthcheck Lambda/agent returns structured JSON (status, backend, latency_ms, last_synced_at) and is exposed to Console metrics
Drift detection runbook and auto-remediation hooks implemented (or a safe alerting path) with sample IAM/ACL remediation scripts
Upgrade/rotation plan validates by running key rotation on a staging cluster without breaking active sessions and includes canary flags
Module has examples for AWS KMS + Vault HA cluster, HSM proxy + Vault, and a hybrid (cloud KMS primary, HSM secondary) configuration
CI pipeline runs terraform validate, unit tests for the lightweight plan rendering, and an integration smoke test in a nightly sandbox
technical_notes: Design uses a 'mux' abstraction: each backend declares a health_probe (http/kms-ping/hsm-session-check), an identity config (client cert, role ARN), and a priority score. The Terraform module generates: (1) central key resource metadata (redwood_kms_key), (2) backend config map stored as encrypted SSM/Vault secret in the bootstrap account, and (3) a small Go-based sidecar (redwood-kms-router) built from internal infra images that negotiates with backends and exposes a health endpoint. Drift detection implemented as a scheduled job that compares Terraform state against runtime registry and emits Prometheus metrics. Avoid storing private key material in Terraform state—only metadata and provider references are tracked.
tasks: Write module inputs/outputs spec and constraints (variables.tf / outputs.tf)
Implement AWS KMS provider wiring and IAM role assumption helper
Prototype HSM proxy connector and session pooling config
Create Vault <-> SecretsManager reconciliation lambda and terraform for scheduled job
Add health probe resources (CloudWatch synthetic check / k8s liveness) and metrics export
Add drift detector and remediation stubs (alerting to #infra and incident playbooks)
Draft canary rollout playbook and add test harness in infra sandbox
Integration tests: rendering, plan-only, and sandbox apply/verify

implementation_risks: Potential vendor HSM SDK incompatibilities and varying latency characteristics; key rotation across heterogeneous backends is complex — we will require a staged rollout and a rollback path that relies on metadata flags rather than destructive key deletion.
